_comment: Performance acceptance floors for link-benchmark (#50), checked by `tools/bench_ci.py floors` in the final `floors` job, after publication, so a violation fails the workflow without blocking the charts. CI-time floors apply only when every build job was warm (exact-input cache hit or 0 zccache misses). The cold reference is run 35451964051 (126 min); a warm run does 14-15 min of work (35470605972). Link-speed floors apply on every run, at each mode's highest measured thread count, skipping noisy cells; they are ~60% of the lowest speedups seen on EPYC 7763 / 9V74 and Xeon 8573C runners, so they catch regressions, not runner variance.

ci_time._comment: work_max_minutes is the sum of the jobs' own recorded times, which is what this workflow controls; total_max_minutes is wall time and also contains the runner queue between jobs (38.5 min wall for 14.4 min of work in run 35470605972), so it is deliberately loose and catches only a real regression.
